Our final end-of-month fundraising deadline is tonight at midnight, and I need your help making sure Keith has the resources to finish strong. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | = | = | | = | = | | = | = Here’s what’s keeping me up at night: Republican megadonors have poured millions into defeating Keith, Trump is attacking him by name, and Sabato’s Crystal Ball still calls this race a “toss-up.” A recent poll found 12% of voters are still undecided—more than enough to decide the outcome. That means we have people to persuade, attacks to answer, and supporters to get to the polls. Our ads and organizing efforts need to keep going through November 3. I wish I could wave a wand and fund all of that. Unfortunately, our budget runs on grassroots contributions, not magic. Keith doesn’t take corporate PAC money. He’s counting on people like you to make sure voters hear the truth about his record before they cast their ballots. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | = | = | | = | = | | = | = Thanks for coming through, Ben Baitman P.S. Forget the ghosts, goblins, witches, and haunted houses.
**Want a real scare? Open your health insurance bill.**
Your premium went up. Your deductible got bigger. Your copay increased. And somehow, despite paying thousands of dollars for health insurance, you're still paying out of pocket when you actually need medical care.
Then comes the next Halloween surprise.
Your longtime doctor is no longer in your network. Your insurance company demands prior authorization. Or you're directed into a major hospital network for something that could have been handled in an independent physician's office.
And sometimes, you discover an additional hospital facility fee on your bill.
**You 're paying more for healthcare and getting less freedom to choose your care.**
That's not a Halloween trick. That's the frightening reality facing too many Connecticut families.
And unlike Halloween, the horror doesn't end November 1.
## The Hospital Network Monster
As a physician, I've watched healthcare change dramatically.
Independent medical practices have increasingly been absorbed into large hospital systems and corporate networks.
What used to be a straightforward visit to your local doctor can now involve centralized scheduling, insurance restrictions, facility fees, and layers of administration.
**Why should a routine office visit cost more simply because a hospital system owns the practice?**
Hospitals play an essential role in providing emergency and complex medical care. But not every patient needs a hospital, and not every medical service belongs in a hospital network.
Independent physicians, community practices, and outpatient facilities are essential to competition, accessibility, and affordability.
When large systems dominate healthcare markets, patients can lose choices and face higher prices.
**Healthcare should be organized around patients --not the financial interests of hospital corporations and insurance companies.**
## The Deductible That Keeps Getting Bigger
Here's another frightening trick.
You pay your health insurance premium every month.
But when you need an MRI, a specialist, a procedure, or even routine treatment, you discover you haven't met your deductible.
So you pay again. .... And again.
**At what point does health insurance stop feeling like protection and start feeling like another expensive monthly bill?**
Families can spend thousands of dollars annually on premiums while still facing substantial out-of-pocket costs.
And when patients delay necessary treatment because they cannot afford it, manageable medical conditions can become serious and expensive emergencies.
That's bad medicine and bad economics.
Insurance should protect families from financial catastrophe--not leave them afraid to use their coverage.
## The Hidden Halloween Trick: Your Employer Pays, But Your Paycheck May Suffer
Some Connecticut workers are fortunate enough to have employers who pay most--or even all--of their health insurance premiums.
You may not feel the full pain when the insurance bill arrives.
**But don 't be fooled. You may still be paying for it through a paycheck that isn't growing.**
When healthcare premiums increase, employers have to find the money somewhere.
And for many businesses, particularly small and midsize employers, healthcare is one of their largest employee benefit expenses.
That money could otherwise help fund higher salaries, bonuses, new jobs, or investments in growing the business.
Instead, more of the employer's compensation budget goes toward insurance and healthcare costs.
**Your employer 's healthcare bill goes up. Your salary stays flat. And you wonder why you're working harder but getting nowhere.**
This is one of the hidden costs of America's healthcare system.
And it's not just employees who suffer.
Small-business owners face difficult choices: absorb higher premiums, pass costs along to customers, reduce benefits, limit hiring, or hold back wage increases.
As a physician and attorney, I understand that this is more than a healthcare problem.
**It 's a wage problem. A jobs problem. And an affordability problem.**
Even if someone else pays your insurance premium, that doesn't mean healthcare inflation isn't costing you money.
**The scariest healthcare bill may be the one you never see --because you're paying for it in raises you never receive.**
That's why lowering healthcare costs isn't just about making medical treatment more affordable.
It's about freeing up money for better wages, more jobs, stronger businesses, and greater economic opportunity throughout Connecticut.
## Washington Has Had 18 Years. Where's the Cure?
My opponent, Congressman Jim Himes, has represented Connecticut's 4th District for 18 years.
During that time, healthcare has remained one of the most serious financial concerns for American families.
The Affordable Care Act expanded insurance coverage and established important protections. But having an insurance card is not the same as having affordable healthcare.
**If you can 't afford your deductible, can't see the doctor you choose, or can't understand your medical bill, the system still needs fixing.**
I've written about the need for change in my previous articles, including _[Hollywood Jim Deserves an Emmy](https://substack.com/redirect/e5e2ad3d-5452-44e4-8150-1820825bfd4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ and my broader discussion of _[The Battle for Connecticut](https://substack.com/redirect/dd42310d-323b-427a-b0e2-a667180fea72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_.
Healthcare is not an isolated problem.
It's part of a larger affordability crisis affecting housing, electricity, transportation, employment, and the ability of families to build a future in Connecticut.
And after 18 years in Washington, I believe it's fair to ask our congressman:
**Where are the results?**
I don't want another speech about how complicated healthcare is.
I want solutions.
## A Doctor's Prescription for Washington
I'm running for Congress because I bring something Washington desperately needs: medical experience, legal training, and practical problem-solving.
As a physician, I understand the challenges patients and doctors face when seeking and delivering care.
As an attorney, I understand how regulations, insurance contracts, corporate consolidation, and federal laws shape the system.
And as a father, I understand how rising costs threaten the next generation's opportunities.
**Here is what I will fight for in Congress:**
**1\. Restore competition and independent medical practices.**
Patients should have meaningful choices beyond the largest hospital systems. We need policies that support independent physicians, community practices, and competition.
**2\. Challenge excessive hospital facility fees.**
The same routine medical service should not automatically cost substantially more simply because it is performed in a hospital-owned setting. Greater price transparency and sensible payment reform can help.
**3\. Reduce premiums, deductibles, and out-of-pocket costs.**
Healthcare reform should be judged by what patients actually pay, not just by the number of people holding insurance cards.
**4\. Cut unnecessary insurance bureaucracy.**
Doctors should spend more time treating patients and less time fighting prior authorizations, claim denials, and administrative obstacles.
**5\. Put prevention before crisis.**
Early diagnosis, preventive care, and better access to physicians can improve outcomes and help avoid costly medical emergencies.
**6\. Protect families from catastrophic medical costs.**
Serious illness should not destroy a family's financial future. Health insurance should provide meaningful protection when patients need it most.
**7\. Make healthcare savings benefit workers and employers.**
Rising employer insurance costs can crowd out wage increases, hiring, and investment. We need to reduce the underlying cost of healthcare so businesses have more room to grow and reward their employees.
**My goal is simple: More healthcare. Less bureaucracy. Lower costs. Greater patient choice.**
## Connecticut Can't Afford Another Two Years of the Same Prescription
Healthcare isn't the only frightening bill Connecticut families face.
Our electricity bills are too high. Housing is increasingly unaffordable. I-95 has become a parking lot. Our trains are aging. And too many young people wonder whether they can afford to remain in Connecticut.
But healthcare is particularly personal.
When your child is sick, you shouldn't have to wonder whether the specialist is in your network.
When your parent needs treatment, you shouldn't have to fight an insurance company for authorization.
When you visit your doctor, you shouldn't be surprised by a hospital facility fee simply because the practice changed ownership.
And when your employer tells you there isn't enough money for a raise, you shouldn't have to wonder how much of that money disappeared into rising insurance premiums.
**We need a healthcare system that treats patients --not one that treats patients like revenue streams.**
As I've discussed in my other articles on [the Goldstein Substack](https://substack.com/redirect/dd42310d-323b-427a-b0e2-a667180fea72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Connecticut needs leadership focused on solving these interconnected problems rather than producing more political theater.
## Connecticut Deserves a Second Opinion
When a patient isn't getting better, a good doctor doesn't keep prescribing the same treatment indefinitely.
* We reassess the diagnosis.
* We examine the evidence.
* We change the treatment.
* And we measure the results.

Washington needs that same approach.
**Jim Himes has had 18 years. Connecticut deserves a second opinion.**
I'm not running to become another television personality or Washington insider.
I'm running to bring medical judgment, legal experience, and practical problem-solving to Congress.
And this Halloween, my message is simple:
**NO MORE TRICKS FROM WASHINGTON.**
**IT 'S TIME TO PUT A DOCTOR IN THE HOUSE.**
* * *
## More From Dr. Michael Goldstein
If you want to understand why I'm running and what I intend to change in Washington, read more of my articles:
**[Hollywood Jim Deserves an Emmy-- Connecticut Deserves Answers](https://substack.com/redirect/e5e2ad3d-5452-44e4-8150-1820825bfd4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

**[The Battle for Connecticut-- More Campaign Commentary](https://substack.com/redirect/dd42310d-323b-427a-b0e2-a667180fea72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Why Connecticut needs stronger representation in Washington, a more competitive economy, affordable energy, and solutions to the challenges facing our families.
**[Read All My Articles on Substack](https://substack.com/redirect/dd42310d-323b-427a-b0e2-a667180fea72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Explore my commentary on healthcare reform, Connecticut's economy, energy policy, infrastructure, government accountability, and the future of our state.
* * *
## 🗳️ Don't Let Another Election Haunt Connecticut
**Early voting continues through Sunday, November 1.**
**Election Day is Tuesday, November 3.**
I'm asking for your vote for Congress in Connecticut's 4th District.
**DR. MICHAEL GOLDSTEIN -- ROW B, POSITION 2B.**
Already voted? Thank you. But your work isn't finished. Please encourage your family, friends, and neighbors to get to the polls.
Every vote matters.
The scariest thing this Halloween isn't a haunted house.
**It 's opening another health insurance bill after two more years of Washington prescribing the same failed treatment.**
**PUT A DOCTOR IN THE HOUSE.**

Our average donation is typically around $27. Over the last couple of weeks, that average gift has dropped down to $22. Our supporters are giving less, and they’re giving less frequently. That’s a problem, and we get it.

But second, we’re hoping that people chip in more than $2 if they can afford to do so. Covering down for the people who can’t give that $10 or $25.
We know you support VoteVets, and we want to make sure you know that we value that support. Everything helps, even donations of $2 — or less.

subject: Good morning and happy Halloween, folks!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Committee to Elect Aaron Ford
body:
Good morning, folks, and happy Halloween!
I’m pumped for today. This morning, we’re kicking off our final get-out-the-vote push.
Our team and volunteers will be knocking on doors, calling voters, and making sure folks across Nevada hear from us before November 3rd.
The latest polling shows that whoever wins over these last-minute voters will likely win this whole thing — so it’s incredibly important that we get our message out to as many Nevadans as possible.
If you can, pitch in $5 this morning to fuel our final weekend of voter outreach. **Every door we knock on, and every call we make could be the one that clinches this race.**

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Facebook just took away two of our biggest tools.
body:
Here’s what Meta’s final-week ad blackout means for us.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, I have bad news, and this one’s a little wonky, so bear with me.
**As of last Tuesday, our campaign can’t launch a single new ad on Facebook or Instagram.**
**[Before I explain what that means, will you chip in $5 right now to help us fill the gap?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261031_2_meta.IrmCrx&refcode=em20261031-2596&amount=5&t=2&akid=2596%2E299639%2EnSO38l)**
Here’s what you need to know: Every election cycle, Meta blocks all new political ads for the final week of the race. **That hits our campaign in two big ways.**
**First, we can’t launch new ads to win over voters.** Whatever ads Greg Abbott already had running can keep running. But through Election Day, we can’t put out a new ad answering his attacks. We can’t respond to breaking news in this race. And we can’t adjust our message on the platforms where millions of Texans spend their time.
**Second, we can’t launch new ads to raise money.** Facebook and Instagram ads asking supporters to chip in are a real part of how we fund this campaign. This month alone, they’ve brought in more than 10% of our online fundraising. Now, right when every dollar matters most, that tool is mostly off the table.
**That means two things have to happen this week.**
**_We have to take our message everywhere Meta can’t stop us:_** streaming TV and YouTube, digital ads on news sites and apps, and TV spots in the markets where this race will be won or lost.
**_And we have to pay for it with grassroots donations from emails like this one**_ , because email is now one of the most important fundraising tools we have left. Every dollar we raise this week goes straight into putting our message in front of the voters who will decide this race.
**[So I’m turning to you, Peter. What we raise from this email will help decide how much ground we can cover this week. Will you chip in $5 or any amount right now to help us keep our message in front of voters through Election Day?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261031_2_meta.IrmCrx&refcode=em20261031-2596&amount=5&t=3&akid=2596%2E299639%2EnSO38l)**

Thank you,
Gina

name: Anika Page
subject: Join us in Jackson for a conversation with Lord Andrew Roberts
body:
Join us in Jackson for a conversation with Lord Andrew Roberts | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/andrewrobertsevent-12855290?e=5703353baa)
---
|
---
| | Good afternoon Friend,
What can Winston Churchill’s life teach us about leadership, courage, and the challenges of our own time? We hope you’ll join the Mississippi Center for Public Policy on **Monday, November 16** , as we welcome acclaimed historian and author **Lord Andrew Roberts** to Jackson for a special luncheon and conversation. Lord Roberts is the author of _Churchill: Walking with Destiny_ , the acclaimed biography of Sir Winston Churchill. Drawing on previously unavailable material, including the wartime diaries of King George VI, his book offers a compelling look at the life and leadership of one of history’s most consequential figures. During our luncheon, Lord Roberts will share insights from his career studying history’s leaders and defining moments. It promises to be an engaging conversation for anyone interested in Churchill, history, and the lessons we can carry into the future.

In 1939, American Lutheran congregations passed a plate to rescue Europeans fleeing Hitler. The charity they built spent eighty years collecting nickels, quilts, and hymns. Today it's called Global Refuge -- rebranded from Lutheran Immigration and Refugee Service (LIRS) in 2024 -- and it collects something else entirely: federal appropriations. According to USAspending.gov, roughly $1.34 billion in federal transactions have flowed to this organization since fiscal 2020.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b0912c44-d013-41ae-87ef-1210781ebca6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Look at the shape of that money. From $67 million to a $340 million peak -- a fivefold climb, nearly a million dollars a day at the top. Then the turn: $230 million, then half that. Two presidents, two business cycles. This wasn't donors getting generous. This was policy.
**Two businesses**
Global Refuge runs two businesses out of Baltimore...

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Elon has spent half a billion dollars (and counting) to try to drown out your vote. Here’s what we can do.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
That’s not democracy. That’s a purchase order.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3074%2E4032634%2EuWDCGj)
---
As of this message, Elon Musk has poured $446 million into these midterm elections — and that’s only the money that’s been disclosed so far. Nearly half a billion dollars (and counting) to help Republicans win. Think about that: the world's first trillionaire — the richest man on Earth — is trying to buy his own government. And why has he done that? Because he’s scared. Elon knows that a Democratic Congress could mean no more tax breaks for billionaires while working families struggle to get by. No more government contracts immediately coming his way. No more loose AI “regulations.” No more dumping millions of dollars into one election to get his way. A Democratic Congress would mean more accountability. And Elon knows that with Democrats in power, he will be held accountable, so he’s trying to buy himself a Congress that won’t ask questions. That’s not democracy. That’s a purchase order. It’s an investment he’s expecting a return on. **Elon Musk has his money. But what we have is the many. A grassroots movement — including you — of people who are sick and tired of our government working great for people like Elon Musk.** On Tuesday, it's voters — not Elon Musk — who will decide the election. Who will determine whether our government answers to working people or the billionaires trying to buy their own government. Elon understands the power of his money, but he’s underestimating the power of people who organize, show up, and make their voices heard. So please, take today and reach out to your friends and family about their plan to vote tomorrow, if they haven’t voted early already. Sign up to knock on doors or make calls to voters tonight, tomorrow, or Tuesday, if you can. Let’s use every minute we have left to counteract his hundreds of millions and show him that the many will defeat the money. Thanks for being part of this, Elizabeth | **Elizabeth Warren is fighting for progressive wins in the 2026 midterms and beyond, and to get Big Money out of our political system once and for all. Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can to help her fight?** | [**DONATE NOW**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/4839?t=8&akid=3074%2E4032634%2EuWDCGj)

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Odysseus
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
There may or may not be a picture of Bailey in his Halloween costume at the end of this email

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3075%2E4032634%2EvV8CgZ)
---
No tricks, NO donation ask. Just a quick note from me (and a Halloween treat at the bottom). I know the flood of emails and texts asking for money is exhausting — and that times are tough right now for so many. I want to be direct and say that I never expect you to be able to respond to each message with a donation — and we’re grateful to have you on this team no matter how much or how often you’re able to donate. Chipping in with a donation is just one way to get involved. It’s important that we do what we can — donate, make calls, put up yard signs, put out messages on social media — because we’re so close in so many races. I’ve kept it up because I’m trying to help — and I know you are too. Take the email I sent two days ago for Abdul El-Sayed: The amount of billionaire-backed Republican PAC money pouring into Michigan to try and defeat him is mind-blowing. The contributions to that email can help keep his ads on television, where he can respond directly to those attacks in this closing week of his race. It can help make sure his field organizers have gas money. It can ensure there’s coffee in the pot and cookies on the table when volunteers get back from door knocking. And it will help build strong teams for elections to come. This team has supported candidates like him across the country: Angie Nixon, Mary Pelota, James Talarico, Juliana Stratton, Peggy Flanagan, Sherrod Brown, Troy Jackson. Good people whose races are on a knife’s edge. Good people who may win or lose based on a handful of votes. And whether they win or lose will have a lot to do with where our nation goes next. On whether we can hold Trump and his administration accountable for their corruption and self-dealing. On whether we can make child care affordable for every family, make the ultrawealthy pay their fair share through a wealth tax, and put real guardrails on AI so giant tech companies can’t put profits ahead of working people. On whether our democracy survives. I don’t want to wake up on the day after the election and talk about the good people who lost by just a bit — and say I wish I’d done a little bit more. And I don’t just want us to win. I want us to win BIG. Big enough that nobody can dismiss the results. Big enough to send a clear message that this country is ready to go in a different direction. So I’m giving it everything I’ve got. I’m grateful for everything that every one of you has already done. And I’m grateful for the chance to be in this fight with you. Happy Halloween, and thanks for being a part of this, Elizabeth P.S. Now here’s a treat: Bailey, a.k.a. Odysseus on his journey home, hopes you’re having a happy and safe Halloween!

---

* * *
**Toplines for the Week**
The midterm story that's been building all year remains clear: this _should_ be an overwhelming victory for Democrats, and therefore for all Americans who oppose Trump. As I showed in last week's _Midterm HQ_ , we're poised for strong outcomes among state legislatures, governors, and the U.S. House, while the Senate is looking as good as could be hoped but still rests on a knife's edge. The newest numbers confirm it, though they've also added some important factors that I'll describe below.
But if you take away nothing else from this final pre-election _Midterm HQ_ or anything you read this weekend, I hope you'll hold on to this: **we need to be prepared for this fight to go well past November 3.**
It gives me no pleasure to write that. In fact, I hope I'm wrong.
However, as the philosopher G.I. Joe taught us, "knowing is half the battle." I'd rather that we be honest and come prepared for a slog than stumble through a haze of hopium into a Trump trap on November 4. So, let's understand that victory will probably be delayed.
But it will not be denied--not if we're ready to fight for it.
